claim: Leigh syndrome (LS) affects 1 in 40,000 births.
source: Leigh syndrome (LS) is the most frequent pediatric mitochondrial disorder, leading to defective mitochondrial energy metabolism. LS affects 1 in 40,000 births (Rahman et al., 1996), although adult onset has also been described (McKelvie et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Rahman et al., 1996.

claim: Adult onset of Leigh syndrome has been described.
source: LS affects 1 in 40,000 births (Rahman et al., 1996), although adult onset has also been described (McKelvie et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to McKelvie et al., 2012.

claim: Mutations in more than 75 genes have been described to cause Leigh syndrome.
source: Mutations in more than 75 genes have been described to cause LS (Lake et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lake et al., 2016.

claim: No effective treatment or cure exists for Leigh syndrome.
source: To date, no effective treatment or cure exists.
evidence: The claim is stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: LS symptoms usually include failure to thrive, hypotonia, rigidity, seizures, ataxia, lactic acidosis, encephalopathy and premature death.
source: Clinically, albeit highly variable, LS symptoms usually include failure to thrive, hypotonia, rigidity, seizures, ataxia, lactic acidosis, encephalopathy and premature death (Rahman et al., 1996; Lake et al., 2016; Sofou et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Rahman et al., 1996; Lake et al., 2016; Sofou et al., 2014.

claim: LS is characterized by restricted anatomical and cellular specificity.
source: LS is characterized by restricted anatomical and cellular specificity (Arii and Tanabe, 2000), a common feature shared by mitochondrial diseases, affecting high energy-requiring tissues such as muscle and brain (Molnar and Kovacs, 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Arii and Tanabe, 2000 and Molnar and Kovacs, 2017.

claim: Mitochondrial diseases affect high energy-requiring tissues such as muscle and brain.
source: LS is characterized by restricted anatomical and cellular specificity (Arii and Tanabe, 2000), a common feature shared by mitochondrial diseases, affecting high energy-requiring tissues such as muscle and brain (Molnar and Kovacs, 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Molnar and Kovacs, 2017.

claim: LS is characterized by the presence of bilateral symmetrical lesions predominantly in the brainstem and basal ganglia.
source: Pathologically, LS is characterized by the presence of bilateral symmetrical lesions predominantly in the brainstem and basal ganglia (Arii and Tanabe, 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Arii and Tanabe, 2000.

claim: Neuronal damage is responsible for most of the fatal symptoms in LS, including respiratory failure and seizures.
source: Neuronal damage is responsible for most of the fatal symptoms, including respiratory failure and seizures (Barends et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Barends et al., 2016.

claim: The identity of the affected cellular populations and the molecular determinants of neuronal vulnerability in LS have not been adequately elucidated.
source: However, the identity of the affected cellular populations and the molecular determinants of neuronal vulnerability have not been adequately elucidated, representing a challenge for the development of efficient treatments.
evidence: The claim is stated as a gap in current knowledge.

claim: Mutations affecting the NDUFS4 subunit of mitochondrial Complex I are commonly associated with a severe, early-onset LS phenotype.
source: Mutations affecting the NDUFS4 subunit of mitochondrial Complex I, a key structural component for the assembly, stability and activity of the complex (Calvaruso et al., 2012), are commonly associated with a severe, early-onset LS phenotype (Ortigoza-Escobar et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Calvaruso et al., 2012 and Ortigoza-Escobar et al., 2016.

claim: NDUFS4 is a key structural component for the assembly, stability and activity of mitochondrial Complex I.
source: Mutations affecting the NDUFS4 subunit of mitochondrial Complex I, a key structural component for the assembly, stability and activity of the complex (Calvaruso et al., 2012), are commonly associated with a severe, early-onset LS phenotype (Ortigoza-Escobar et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Calvaruso et al., 2012.

claim: A late-onset case of LS has been recently reported.
source: Although a late-onset case of LS has been recently reported (Bris et al., 2017), prognosis is usually poor and most of the patients die in early childhood (Sofou et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Bris et al., 2017.

claim: Most LS patients die in early childhood.
source: Although a late-onset case of LS has been recently reported (Bris et al., 2017), prognosis is usually poor and most of the patients die in early childhood (Sofou et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sofou et al., 2014.

claim: Ndufs4KO mice develop a fatal encephalomyopathy that recapitulates the classical signs of LS.
source: Animals with a global deletion of Ndufs4 (Ndufs4KO mice) develop a fatal encephalomyopathy, which recapitulates the classical signs of LS, including motor alterations, respiratory deficits, epilepsy and premature death (Quintana et al., 2010; Kruse et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Quintana et al., 2010 and Kruse et al., 2008.

claim: Ndufs4KO mice exhibit motor alterations, respiratory deficits, epilepsy and premature death.
source: Animals with a global deletion of Ndufs4 (Ndufs4KO mice) develop a fatal encephalomyopathy, which recapitulates the classical signs of LS, including motor alterations, respiratory deficits, epilepsy and premature death (Quintana et al., 2010; Kruse et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Quintana et al., 2010 and Kruse et al., 2008.

claim: The dorsal brainstem, particularly the vestibular nucleus (VN), plays a pivotal role in disease manifestation and progression in Ndufs4KO mice.
source: Behavioral and neuropathological characterization of Ndufs4KO mice revealed the pivotal role of the dorsal brainstem, particularly the vestibular nucleus (VN), in disease manifestation and progression (Quintana et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Quintana et al., 2012.

claim: The genetic identity of the neuronal populations and circuitries involved in the symptoms of Ndufs4KO mice have not yet been identified.
source: However, the genetic identity of the neuronal populations and circuitries involved in the plethora of symptoms observed have not yet been identified.
evidence: The claim is stated as a gap in current knowledge.

claim: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice have a median lifespan of 67 days with a mortality rate of 90% at postnatal day 128.
source: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice had a median lifespan of 67 days with a mortality rate of 90% at postnatal day (P) 128.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice have a median lifespan of 60 days with 90% mortality at P70.
source: Similarly, Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice had a median lifespan of 60 days (90% mortality at P70) (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript and Figure 1B.

claim: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice show reduced body weight gain in male and female mice.
source: This premature death was preceded by a reduction in body weight gain in male and female mice of both genotypes (Figure 1C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C-F.

claim: Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice show reduced body weight gain in male and female mice.
source: This premature death was preceded by a reduction in body weight gain in male and female mice of both genotypes (Figure 1C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C-F.

claim: At 7 weeks of age for females and 9 weeks of age for males, Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice stopped gaining weight.
source: At 7 weeks of age for females and 9 weeks of age for males, Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice stopped gaining weight, which resulted in an overall reduction in body weight when compared to age-matched controls (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and 1D.

claim: Male and female Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice body weight reached a plateau 2–3 weeks before manifesting a sudden unexpected death.
source: Similarly, male and female Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice body weight reached a plateau 2–3 weeks before manifesting a sudden unexpected death (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and 1F.

claim: Both Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO and Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice are significantly smaller than their littermate controls.
source: Both Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO and Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice were also significantly smaller than their littermate controls (Figure 1G–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G-H.

claim: The lack of weight gain and reduced size in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO and Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice appeared to be due to decreased food intake.
source: This lack of weight gain and reduced size appeared to be due to decreased food intake in both genotypes (Figure 1I,J); however, this was not significantly different when food consumption was normalized to body weight (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1I, 1J, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Food consumption normalized to body weight was not significantly different in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO and Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice compared to controls.
source: This lack of weight gain and reduced size appeared to be due to decreased food intake in both genotypes (Figure 1I,J); however, this was not significantly different when food consumption was normalized to body weight (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice present body tremor as early as at 5 weeks.
source: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice presented body tremor and a decline in balance as early as at 5 weeks (early stage of the disease), which dramatically worsened as the disease progressed.
evidence: The claim is supported by observational data from clinical evaluation.

claim: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice show a decline in balance as early as at 5 weeks.
source: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice presented body tremor and a decline in balance as early as at 5 weeks (early stage of the disease), which dramatically worsened as the disease progressed.
evidence: The claim is supported by observational data from clinical evaluation.

claim: In a mid-stage of the disease, Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice show increased body tremor and a prominent decline in balance and motor coordination.
source: In a mid-stage of the disease, mice increased body tremor and showed a prominent decline in balance and motor coordination (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by observational data presented in Table 1.

claim: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice exhibit ataxia and a progressive loss of the righting and hindlimb extension reflexes (clasping).
source: Subsequently, animals started exhibiting ataxia and a progressive loss of the righting and hindlimb extension reflexes (clasping) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by observational data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: At a late stage of the disease, Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice show increased tremor and are completely docile and hypotonic.
source: At a late stage of the disease, these mice showed increased tremor, were completely docile and hypotonic (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by observational data presented in Table 1.

claim: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice have difficulty maintaining a regular breathing pattern at an early stage of the disease.
source: Animals also had difficulty maintaining a regular breathing pattern at an early stage of the disease.
evidence: The claim is supported by observational data from clinical evaluation.

claim: Breathing abnormalities in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice worsen as the disease progresses.
source: These breathing abnormalities worsened as the disease progressed with mice presenting noticeably shorter and deeper respirations at advanced stages of the disease (Video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by observational data shown in Video 1.

claim: About 40% of Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice develop hindlimb dragging and eventually hindlimb paralysis at a late stage of the disease (over P60).
source: Furthermore, at a late stage of the disease (over P60), about 40% of Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO developed hindlimb dragging and eventually hindlimb paralysis.
evidence: The claim is supported by observational data from clinical evaluation.

claim: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice show increased glial reactivity but no neuronal loss in the spinal cord.
source: We observed increased glial reactivity but no neuronal loss in the spinal cord of these mice when compared to Vglut2:Ndufs4cCT mice, which was determined by immunoblot analysis of spinal cord lysates from Vglut2:Ndufs4cCT and Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice using antibodies against GFAP (glial fibrillary acidic protein), Iba-1 (ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1) and NSE (neuronal specific enolase) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Glial reactivity in the spinal cords of Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice that exhibited hindlimb dragging was confirmed by immunofluorescence analysis.
source: This glial reactivity was further confirmed by immunofluorescence analysis using anti-GFAP and anti-Iba-1 antibodies in the spinal cords of the Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice that exhibited hindlimb dragging (Figure 1—figure supplement 3, top panels).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: No signs of demyelination or immune cell infiltration were observed in the spinal cords of Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice.
source: However, no signs of demyelination or immune cell infiltration were observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 3, mid and bottom panels).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Late-stage Ndufs4-deficient mice present overt lesions in brainstem (namely vestibular nucleus (VN), cerebellar fastigial nucleus (FN) and inferior olive (IO)), olfactory bulb and basal ganglia.
source: Accordingly, late-stage Ndufs4-deficient mice present overt lesions in brainstem (namely vestibular nucleus (VN), cerebellar fastigial nucleus (FN) and inferior olive (IO)), olfactory bulb and basal ganglia (Quintana et al., 2010; Quintana et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2017a).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Quintana et al., 2010; Quintana et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2017a.

claim: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice show marked glial reactivity in VN, IO and FN.
source: Analysis of these sections showed marked glial reactivity in VN, IO and FN (Figure 2A, C; Figure 2—figure supplement 1), accompanied by increased caspase eight activation in affected areas (such as the VN) in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice (Figure 2E,F), recapitulating most of the neuroinflammatory profile described for the global Ndufs4KO mice (Quintana et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A, 2C, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice show increased caspase eight activation in affected areas such as the VN.
source: Analysis of these sections showed marked glial reactivity in VN, IO and FN (Figure 2A, C; Figure 2—figure supplement 1), accompanied by increased caspase eight activation in affected areas (such as the VN) in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice (Figure 2E,F), recapitulating most of the neuroinflammatory profile described for the global Ndufs4KO mice (Quintana et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2E and 2F.

claim: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice recapitulate most of the neuroinflammatory profile described for the global Ndufs4KO mice.
source: Analysis of these sections showed marked glial reactivity in VN, IO and FN (Figure 2A, C; Figure 2—figure supplement 1), accompanied by increased caspase eight activation in affected areas (such as the VN) in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice (Figure 2E,F), recapitulating most of the neuroinflammatory profile described for the global Ndufs4KO mice (Quintana et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison to data from Quintana et al., 2010.

claim: Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice present marked microglial and astroglial reactivity in primarily GABAergic nuclei such as the external globus pallidus (GPe) in the basal ganglia and the substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr).
source: In contrast, Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice presented a more restricted glial reactivity pattern, including marked microglial and astroglial reactivity in primarily GABAergic nuclei such as the external globus pallidus (GPe) in the basal ganglia and the substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr) (Figure 2B, D), without affecting neighboring non-GABAergic areas like the dopaminergic substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2B and 2D.

claim: Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice do not show glial reactivity in neighboring non-GABAergic areas like the dopaminergic substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc).
source: In contrast, Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice presented a more restricted glial reactivity pattern, including marked microglial and astroglial reactivity in primarily GABAergic nuclei such as the external globus pallidus (GPe) in the basal ganglia and the substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr) (Figure 2B, D), without affecting neighboring non-GABAergic areas like the dopaminergic substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The olfactory bulb shows increased immunoreactivity for GFAP and Iba-1 in Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice when compared to control mice.
source: Other prominently GABAergic areas such as the olfactory bulb also showed increased immunoreactivity for GFAP and Iba-1 in Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice when compared to control mice (Figure 2B,D; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2B, 2D, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: In a percentage of Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice, prominent microglial reactivity with Purkinje neuron loss was observed in the cerebellar vermis and flocculus.
source: In a percentage of Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice, prominent microglial reactivity with Purkinje neuron loss (as assessed by calbindin staining) was also observed in the cerebellar vermis and flocculus (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Normal Slc17a6 (Vglut2) transcript abundance was observed in the VN of late-stage Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice.
source: Normal Slc17a6 (Vglut2) or Gad2 transcript abundance was observed in the VN and OB of late-stage Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO or Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice, respectively, suggesting preservation of Ndufs4-deficient neuronal populations (Figure 2G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Normal Gad2 transcript abundance was observed in the OB of Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice.
source: Normal Slc17a6 (Vglut2) or Gad2 transcript abundance was observed in the VN and OB of late-stage Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO or Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice, respectively, suggesting preservation of Ndufs4-deficient neuronal populations (Figure 2G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Normal transcript abundance of Slc17a6 (Vglut2) and Gad2 in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO and Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice suggests preservation of Ndufs4-deficient neuronal populations.
source: Normal Slc17a6 (Vglut2) or Gad2 transcript abundance was observed in the VN and OB of late-stage Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO or Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice, respectively, suggesting preservation of Ndufs4-deficient neuronal populations (Figure 2G,H).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2G and 2H.

claim: Starting at P40, Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice showed impaired rotarod performance when compared to control littermates.
source: Starting at P40, and concurring with the onset of clinical signs, Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice showed impaired rotarod performance when compared to control littermates (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by rotarod test data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice present a progressive decline in motor coordination.
source: While control mice maintained rotarod performance, Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice failed to properly execute the task, presenting a progressive decline in motor coordination, in line with the clinical phenotype.
evidence: The claim is supported by rotarod test data.

claim: No differences in rotarod performance were observed in Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice compared to control littermates.
source: Conversely, and in agreement with the lack of apparent clinical signs, no differences in rotarod performance were observed in Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice compared to control littermates (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by rotarod test data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice show a hypoactive phenotype as assessed by a reduction in the total distance traveled and the speed of exploratory movement in the open-field test.
source: Exposure to a novel environment revealed a hypoactive phenotype in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice as assessed by a reduction in the total distance traveled and the speed of exploratory movement in the open-field test (Figure 3C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by open-field test data shown in Figure 3C-E.

claim: The severity of the hypoactive phenotype in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice positively correlates with age and disease stage.
source: The severity of this phenotype in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice positively correlated with age and disease stage (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by open-field test data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: No significant differences were observed in either distance traveled or speed in the open-field test between Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice and their respective controls.
source: In contrast, no significant differences were observed in either distance traveled or speed in the open-field test between Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice and their respective controls (Figure 3F–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by open-field test data shown in Figure 3F-H.

claim: No differences in the innervation of neuromuscular junctions were observed in the gastrocnemius muscle of either Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO or Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice.
source: No differences in the innervation of neuromuscular junctions were observed in the gastrocnemius muscle of either Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO or Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice (Figure 3I–K), suggesting a central origin of the motor phenotype.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3I-K.

claim: The motor phenotype in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO and Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice has a central origin.
source: No differences in the innervation of neuromuscular junctions were observed in the gastrocnemius muscle of either Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO or Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice (Figure 3I–K), suggesting a central origin of the motor phenotype.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on neuromuscular junction data.

claim: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice exhibit erratic plethysmographic recordings.
source: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice exhibited erratic plethysmographic recordings (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by plethysmography data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The frequency of respiration (fR) is markedly reduced in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice at a mid-stage (P40-P60) of the disease and worsens as disease progresses.
source: In these mice, the frequency of respiration (fR) was markedly reduced at a mid-stage (P40-P60) of the disease and worsened as disease progressed (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by plethysmography data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Tidal volume (VT) is increased in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice at a mid-stage of the disease and becomes significantly larger than in Vglut2:Ndufs4cCT at late disease stages.
source: In addition, significant differences were also seen in the volume of air inspired by the animal during one breath (tidal volume, VT). VT was increased in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice at a mid-stage of the disease and became significantly larger than in Vglut2:Ndufs4cCT at late disease stages (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by plethysmography data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice do not exhibit irregular plethysmographic traces and have breathing patterns (fR and VT) that do not differ from controls.
source: In contrast, Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice did not exhibit irregular plethysmographic traces and had breathing patterns (fR and VT) that did not differ from controls (Figure 4B and E–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by plethysmography data shown in Figure 4B and E-F.

claim: The motor impairment and respiratory deficits observed in the Ndufs4KO mouse are mediated by Vglut2-expressing excitatory neuronal populations.
source: These data reveal that the motor impairment and respiratory deficits observed in the Ndufs4KO mouse are mediated by Vglut2-expressing excitatory neuronal populations.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the respiratory and motor data from Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice.

claim: Neuronal inactivation of Ndufs4 in the VN promotes breathing abnormalities.
source: We have shown that neuronal inactivation of Ndufs4 in the VN promotes breathing abnormalities (Quintana et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Quintana et al., 2012.

claim: The firing rate for vestibular Vglut2-expressing neurons from Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice is not significantly different than controls when mice are at rest.
source: Electrophysiological recordings in vivo showed that the firing rate for vestibular Vglut2-expressing neurons from Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice was not significantly different than controls when mice were at rest.
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo electrophysiology data.

claim: When mice are actively moving in the open-field, Vglut2-expressing VN neurons in control mice approximately double their firing rate to about 40 Hz but the experimental group does not.
source: However, when the mice were actively moving in the open-field, the Vglut2-expressing VN neurons in the control mice approximately doubled their firing rate to about 40 Hz but the experimental group did not (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo electrophysiology data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The failure of VN glutamatergic neurons in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice to respond to motor activity may account for the breathing abnormalities.
source: The failure of VN glutamatergic neurons in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice to respond to motor activity may account for the breathing abnormalities.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on electrophysiology data.

claim: Dysregulation of body temperature homeostasis, such as hypothermia, is commonly observed in LS patients.
source: Dysregulation of body temperature homeostasis, such as hypothermia, is commonly observed in LS patients (Finsterer, 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Finsterer, 2008.

claim: Global Ndufs4KO mice present reduced body temperature starting at P30.
source: Accordingly, global Ndufs4KO mice present reduced body temperature starting at P30 (Quintana et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Quintana et al., 2010.

claim: Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice present normal resting body temperature during early life, decreasing only as the disease progresses to mid-late stage (P40 onwards).
source: Hence, using telemetric temperature monitoring, we observed that Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO presented normal resting body temperature during early life, decreasing only as the disease progressed to mid-late stage (P40 onwards, Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by telemetric temperature data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice show a severe reduction in resting body temperature as early as P20-P30, which is maintained at all time points analyzed.
source: In contrast, we identified a severe reduction in resting body temperature of Gad2:Ndufs4cKO as early as P20-P30, which was maintained at all time points analyzed (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by telemetric temperature data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: GABAergic neurons play a central role in central body temperature regulation in the context of Ndufs4 deficiency.
source: Therefore, our results suggest a central role of GABAergic neurons in central body temperature regulation in the context of Ndufs4 deficiency.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on temperature data from Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice.

claim: Spontaneous seizure-like events were observed in Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice during routine husbandry practices.
source: In Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice, spontaneous seizure-like events were observed during routine husbandry practices such as lifting the animal by the tail or cage cleaning (Video 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by observational data shown in Video 2.

claim: All deaths in Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice consistently followed a severe generalized tonic-clonic convulsion.
source: Analysis of the recordings revealed that all deaths in Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice consistently followed a severe generalized tonic-clonic convulsion.
evidence: The claim is supported by video recording analysis.

claim: Spontaneous, sporadic or lethal seizures were not observed in either controls or Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice at any stage of the disease.
source: In contrast, spontaneous, sporadic or lethal seizures were not observed in either controls (data not shown) or Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice at any stage of the disease (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by observational data and EEG-EMG recordings shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Seizures in Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice are mostly generalized and of multiple semiology (unilateral, primary bilateral, secondary bilateral or alternating).
source: Detailed visualization and analysis of the images unveiled that seizures in Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice were mostly generalized and of multiple semiology (unilateral, primary bilateral, secondary bilateral or alternating).
evidence: The claim is supported by video recording analysis.

claim: Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice show the presence of spontaneous generalized tonic-clonic (GTC) seizures.
source: Subsequent electroencephalographic (EEG) and electromyographic (EMG) characterization showed the presence of spontaneous generalized tonic-clonic (GTC) seizures (Figure 7A), interictal spikes and myoclonic seizures in Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice (Figure 7B–C), which are hallmarks of epilepsy in mitochondrial disorders (Rahman, 2015), with 40–60% of mitochondrial disease patients manifesting seizures (Koenig, 2008; El Sabbagh et al., 2010; Canafoglia et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by EEG-EMG data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice show interictal spikes and myoclonic seizures.
source: Subsequent electroencephalographic (EEG) and electromyographic (EMG) characterization showed the presence of spontaneous generalized tonic-clonic (GTC) seizures (Figure 7A), interictal spikes and myoclonic seizures in Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice (Figure 7B–C), which are hallmarks of epilepsy in mitochondrial disorders (Rahman, 2015), with 40–60% of mitochondrial disease patients manifesting seizures (Koenig, 2008; El Sabbagh et al., 2010; Canafoglia et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by EEG-EMG data shown in Figure 7B-C.

claim: Interictal spikes and myoclonic seizures are hallmarks of epilepsy in mitochondrial disorders.

evidence: The claim is supported by LFP recording data shown in Figure 7D.

source: Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice were highly sensitive to temperature compared to Gad2:Ndufs4cCT mice, with some mice displaying seizures already at basal temperature.

claim: Drug-treated Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice showed a median survival of 63, 62 and 66 days for levetiracetam, perampanel and carbamazepine, respectively, which was not statistically significant when compared to the median lifespan of vehicle-treated mice (60 days).

claim: Mice lacking Ndufs4 in cholinergic neurons (ChAT:Ndufs4cKO) show no effect on survival, body weight, or motor function.

claim: Decreased food intake in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO and Gad2:Ndufs4cKO mice was not significantly different when food consumption was normalized to body weight.

claim: Gene expression analysis in the brainstem of late-stage Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice showed that differentially expressed mRNAs were, for the most part, upregulated.
source: Gene expression analysis in the brainstem of late-stage (over P68) Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice using Illumina Beadchips (MouseRef-8 V2; Illumina) showed that differentially expressed (DE) mRNAs were, for the most part, upregulated in Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice (p<0.05, Fold Change > 2) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Differentially expressed genes in the brainstem of Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice include transcripts directly involved in the regulation of the immune system such as chemokines and their receptors, toll-like receptors, complement proteins, surface antigens, and markers of the myeloid cell lineage.

evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data.

claim: Functional enrichment analysis of differentially expressed mRNAs in the brainstem of Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice showed that the top 10 most overrepresented Gene Ontology categories were all related to defense and immune responses.
source: Functional enrichment analysis of differentially expressed mRNAs (1.4-fold or higher) using overrepresentation analysis (ORA) (Wang et al., 2017) showed that the top 10 most overrepresented Gene Ontology (GO) categories (biological process, non-redundant) were all related to defense and immune responses, and also uncovered components of the adaptive immune response (GO:0002250; p=2.0177e-12, FDR = 7.2033e-10) including 'leucocyte mediated immunity' (GO:0002443; p=1.7533e-12, FDR = 7.2033e-10) and 'myeloid leukocyte activation' (GO:0002274; p=8.7458e-10, FDR = 9.0537e-8) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by functional enrichment analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Deconvolution analysis revealed a gene expression profile consistent with an increased proportion of proinflammatory CD4 cells, dendritic cells, mast cells and macrophages, and an underrepresentation of CD4 Th2 cells, CD8 cells and NK cells in the brainstem of Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice compared to controls.
source: This analysis revealed a gene expression profile consistent with an increased proportion of proinflammatory CD4 cells (Follicular cells, Th1, Th17 and Treg), dendritic cells, mast cells and macrophages, and an underrepresentation of CD4 Th2 cells, CD8 cells and NK cells in the brainstem of Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice compared to controls, showing that Ndufs4 deficiency in glutamatergic neurons promotes a neuroinflammatory environment that involves a commitment to distinct proinflammatory TH cell lineages and a defined profile of tissue defense cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by deconvolution analysis of gene expression data.

claim: Ndufs4 deficiency in glutamatergic neurons promotes a neuroinflammatory environment that involves a commitment to distinct proinflammatory TH cell lineages and a defined profile of tissue defense cells.
source: This analysis revealed a gene expression profile consistent with an increased proportion of proinflammatory CD4 cells (Follicular cells, Th1, Th17 and Treg), dendritic cells, mast cells and macrophages, and an underrepresentation of CD4 Th2 cells, CD8 cells and NK cells in the brainstem of Vglut2:Ndufs4cKO mice compared to controls, showing that Ndufs4 deficiency in glutamatergic neurons promotes a neuroinflammatory environment that involves a commitment to distinct proinflammatory TH cell lineages and a defined profile of tissue defense cells.
